The Story in Maps

The Atlas

A thousand years of borders, rivers, rails, and weather — the shape of Russian history, drawn. Step through the empire's rise and fall, then read the land itself.

The empire in seven maps

Seven snapshots across four centuries — watch a landlocked tsardom become the largest contiguous empire on earth, then contract to the Federation of today. Use the years, the arrows, or your keyboard's ← →.

The land & the lines

Beyond the borders: the belts of tundra, forest, and steppe; the rivers that were the first roads; the rails that remade the east; the great battles; and the brutal swing of a continental winter and summer.

Maps are schematic — historical extents approximated onto modern outlines, for orientation rather than precision. Part of the Russian History guide.
